# Navier–Stokes Lean Audit: summary

**Preliminary. No mathematician has reviewed any of this yet.** Every entry is a place where the paper and the Lean say different things, not a claimed error. This page is generated by `audit/report.py`; the full data is in the CSVs next to it, and `report.html` (download it and open it locally) has every difference with quotes. How it works: [METHODOLOGY.md](../METHODOLOGY.md).

Paper: [navier-stokes.pdf](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf) · Lean: [openai/NavierStokesAndEuler](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler) at `f9e8bc5b38b6`

## At a glance

- **Paper → Lean map:** 77 of 80 numbered results matched by all 3 samples; 3 targets without a 3-of-3 match (results and proof steps together). Matches move between runs; see CHANGES-v0.2.md.
- **Compared in detail:** 67 (paper result or proof step, Lean declaration) pairs from the Section 8 pilot, Lemma 10.5 and selected proof steps.
- **Differences:** 1,712 grouped. 442 have overlapping citations from all 3 samples; 206 of those were confirmed by adjudication to describe the same difference. Most are naming, or the Lean spelling out conditions the paper leaves implicit.
- **Retrospective recovery:** Lemma 8.6: 3 of 3 samples at the expected Lean lines (the same check fires on 0 of 66 other pairs); (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: 3 of 3 samples at the expected Lean lines (the same check fires on 60 of 66 other pairs). The targets were chosen because of the paper that published them (see below).
- **Static checks** (source text only, nothing compiled): 0 uses of `sorry`, `axiom`, `admit`, `native_decide` or `unsafe` in the 816 files under `NavierStokes/`; 474 theorems are copies of each other in 187 groups (57 copies unreferenced). See [duplicate_statements.csv](duplicate_statements.csv).
- **Start with** [review_shortlist.md](review_shortlist.md): the differences most worth an expert's time.

## Retrospective recovery of two published discrepancies

The two discrepancies Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen published ([arXiv:2610.08144](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08144)). These results were put on the target list because of that paper, so this checks recovery when the tool is pointed at them, not discovery; the prompts never describe the discrepancies.

Each target is a place, not a wording: the Lean declaration, the lines of the expression the discrepancy is about, and the difference types that count. A sample hits it if it reported a difference of one of those types citing those lines. The control runs the same check over the statements of every other pair compared, to show how often it fires by chance.

- **Lemma 8.6** · `SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.inverse_finiteJets` · [SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean:868](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean#L868) · stronger-bound: **3 of 3 samples**. Control: the same check fires on 0 of the other 66 pairs, and on 0.0% of 606 windows along their statements.
  - 3/3 overlapping, adjudicated 3/3 · [SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean:868](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean#L868): The paper's derivative loss is m+4, while the Lean theorem assumes n+5 and concludes n.
- **(10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5** · `PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound` · [R3/PressureFlux.lean:587-588](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/R3/PressureFlux.lean#L587-L588) · stronger-bound / weaker-bound / other: **3 of 3 samples**. Control: the same check fires on 60 of the other 66 pairs, and on 37.5% of 530 windows along their statements.
  - 1/3 overlapping, adjudicated n/a/3 · [R3/PressureFlux.lean:588](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/R3/PressureFlux.lean#L588): If the quantities correspond, the Lean bound has an additional positive 1/R^2 contribution not present in the paper's displayed bound.
  - 1/3 overlapping, adjudicated n/a/3 · [R3/PressureFlux.lean:587](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/R3/PressureFlux.lean#L587): The paper's cutoff notation is χ_R/φ_R; the Lean statement uses ComparisonCutoffs.weight/cutoff.
  - 2/3 overlapping, adjudicated 2/3 · [R3/PressureFlux.lean:587-588](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/R3/PressureFlux.lean#L587-L588): The algebraic form of the first part of the bound differs.
  - 2/3 overlapping, adjudicated 0/3 · [R3/PressureFlux.lean:588](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/R3/PressureFlux.lean#L588): The Lean expression includes an additional 1/R^2 summand.
